---
title: Chroma Key
description: Remove a background colour, such as a green screen, so whatever is on the tracks behind shows through.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Chroma Key removes one colour from a clip, such as a green screen, so whatever is on the tracks behind shows through.

<AtAGlance
  keys="⎋"
  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Chroma Key"
  tools="set_video"
/>

## Key out a color

<Steps>

1. Put the clip on a track in front of what should show through, and select it.

2. In the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, open the **Chroma Key** section. It comes after **Corner Radius** and is shut by default.

3. Choose **Pick from Canvas** and click the background in the preview. That sets the colour and turns the key on. Or tick **Key out a color**, which keys pure green.

4. Adjust [**Tolerance**](#tolerance), [**Softness**](#softness) and [**Spill**](#spill) until the edges look right.

</Steps>

Turning the key on gives pure green at 20 % Tolerance, 10 % Softness and 50 % Spill. Every row but **Pick from Canvas** stays dimmed until the key is on. The section's header reads "off", or the Tolerance as a percentage. **Reset** takes the key off the clip.

The section is there for clips of a video file, image clips and freeze frames. Text, shape and graphic clips don't have it. With several clips selected, an edit keys all of them.

## Key color

The colour to remove. It starts as pure green, and the swatch takes any colour. The opacity in the colour panel has no effect here, because a key colour has none.

## Pick from Canvas

Choose **Pick from Canvas** and the preview reads "Click to pick the key color · Esc to cancel". One click on the picture sets **Key Color**. The button works with the key off, and a pick turns it on.

A pick reads the clip as the key sees it, without the clip's own key, grade and opacity. So picking again reads the same green the first pick did, even though that green is now a hole. A clip in front of it at that point still covers it, and you get what's visible there.

Picking again changes only the colour. It keeps the **Tolerance**, **Softness** and **Spill** you set.

To cancel, press the button again, press <kbd>⎋</kbd> or change the selection.

| If | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| You click outside the picture | Frame Job beeps and stays ready for another click |
| You click where the canvas holds nothing | Frame Job beeps and changes nothing |
| The selection changes while the frame is being read | Frame Job beeps and changes nothing |

Only one canvas tool is ready at a time. **Pick from Canvas** ends [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)'s **Place on Canvas**, [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) and the [qualifier's Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/).

## Tune the key

Start with **Tolerance** to clear the background, then **Softness** for the edge, then **Spill** for any fringe of the key colour.

### Tolerance

How far from the key colour still counts as background. Everything that close is removed completely. Raise it if patches of background remain, and lower it if the key eats into your subject.

The range is 0 to 100 %, and the default is 20 %. The quick picks are 0, 10, 20, 40 and 60.

### Softness

How gradual the edge of the key is. Past **Tolerance**, the picture fades back in over this distance, so a low value gives a hard edge.

The range is 0 to 100 %, and the default is 10 %. The quick picks are 0, 5, 10, 25 and 50.

### Spill

How much of the key colour is removed from the edges that remain. Pixels in the soft edge are pulled toward a grey of their own brightness, which takes out a green fringe. It works only in that edge, so with **Softness** at 0 it has almost nothing to act on.

The range is 0 to 100 %, and the default is 50 %. The quick picks are 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100.

## Animate the key

With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Key Color**, **Tolerance**, **Softness** and **Spill** set the value at the action's end and animate toward it. The colour blends through the OKLab colour space along the action. **Pick from Canvas** also sends its colour to the action's end.

## Good to know

- The key runs before the grade, so [grading a clip](/color/color-tab/) doesn't change what's keyed. A [camera log](/hdr/camera-log/) conversion and the [source conversion](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/) come first, so the key sees the converted picture.
- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) leaves the key on.
- How a key behaves when a project switches between SDR and HDR is on [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).

## Related

- [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/)
- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)
- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)

---
title: Remove Background
description: Keep the person in a video or picture and make the rest transparent, with no green screen, upload or key.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Remove Background keeps the person in a video or picture and makes the rest transparent, so whatever is on the tracks behind shows through. You don't need a green screen.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Background"
  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Background"
  tools={['set_video', 'analyze_cutout', 'get_media_analysis']}
  needs="Nothing. The masks are made on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

<Shot
  name="05i-clip-background.inspector"
  alt="The Background section of the inspector, open, with its summary reading Analyzing 0 %. Remove background is ticked, Background reads Remove, Edge is at 0.00, Feather is at 0%, Status reads Analyzing 0 %, and an Analyze Now button sits below."
/>

## Turn it on

Select a clip and choose **Clip ▸ Remove Background**, or tick **Remove background** in the Clip tab's **Background** section. The menu item has no keyboard shortcut. Frame Job starts making the [masks](#how-the-masks-are-made) straight away, and you don't need to do anything else.

It works on clips of a video file with pictures, freeze frames of one, and image clips. Text, shape, graphic, adjustment and nest clips can't be cut out, and the section appears only when every selected clip can.

With several clips selected:

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Clip ▸ Remove Background** | When every clip that can be cut out already is, it turns them all off. Otherwise it turns on the ones without it, and each clip that has it keeps its own values. Selected clips that can't be cut out are left alone. |
| **Remove background** checkbox | Ticking it gives each clip without it the defaults. Unticking it removes it from all of them. |

The menu item shows a check when every target is cut out, a dash when some are, and nothing when none are. It's dimmed when no selected clip can be cut out. Either way, the change is one undo step, **Remove Background**.

The section comes right after **Chroma Key** and is shut by default. Its header reads "off", the [Status](#status), or "on" with several clips selected. **Reset** turns Remove Background off.

**Subject**, **Background**, **Edge** and **Feather** stay dimmed until every selected clip has Remove Background on. A selection where only some clips have it keeps them dimmed.

## Tune the cut-out

### Subject

This row shows only when every selected clip is a picture. See [Pictures](#pictures).

| Choice | What it keeps |
| --- | --- |
| **Person** (default) | The person |
| **Foreground** | The foreground subject, whatever it is: a person, a pet or an object |

It reads mixed when the selected pictures differ. A clip of a video file or a freeze frame always keeps the person.

### Background

**Remove**, the default, draws the subject alone. **Keep** draws the whole clip, while the subject still counts as a shape, and the masks are made either way.

**Keep** is how a title goes behind a person in frame, and it's what [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) gives a clip with no cut-out.

### Edge

Pulls the outline in or pushes it out. Below 0 pulls in, and above 0 pushes out. The range is −1 to 1, the default is 0, and the quick picks are −0.5, −0.25, 0, 0.25 and 0.5.

A mask is more or less sure of each point in the picture. **Edge** sets how sure it has to be. With **Feather** at 0:

| Edge | The outline sits where the mask is |
| --- | --- |
| −1 | 7/8 sure it's the person |
| −0.5 | 3/4 sure |
| 0 | Half sure |
| 0.5 | 1/4 sure |
| 1 | 1/8 sure |

Across a band of pixels where the mask fades from background to person, **Edge** at −1 or 1 moves the outline about three eighths of the band's width. Raising **Edge** never removes anything a lower value kept.

### Feather

How soft the outline is. The range is 0 to 100 %, the default is 0 %, and the quick picks are 0, 10, 25 and 50.

### Inside an action

With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Edge** and **Feather** set the value at the action's end and animate toward it. **Background** switches at the action's end, and its row shows "at end".

The **Remove background** checkbox and **Subject** always change the clip itself, even with an action selected, so their rows show ⊘. You can't turn a cut-out off at the end of an action.

## How the masks are made

A mask is the outline of the subject in one frame. You never start this yourself. Turning Remove Background on, or changing what a cut-out clip plays, asks for the frames that clip needs, and Frame Job makes them in the background while you go on working.

Masks are made on this Mac with Vision's person segmentation at its balanced setting. Nothing is uploaded, and no key is needed. They're kept per media in the project's cache, so a frame that's been analysed is never analysed again. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#person-masks).

Until a frame has its mask, the clip draws whole in the preview. A paused frame redraws by itself as masks land, and a playing preview picks them up on its next frame.

### Status

**Status** says where the clip's masks stand, and why a clip is drawing whole.

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Analyzing N %** | The masks are being made. The figure stops at 99 until they're done. |
| **Ready** | Every frame the clip plays has its mask. |
| **No person found** | Every frame was looked at and no person is in the clip, so it draws whole. A frame counts as holding a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half. |
| **No subject found** | A picture with **Subject** set to **Foreground** was looked at and no subject was found, so it draws whole. |
| **Failed:** and the reason | The masks couldn't be made. The media file may be missing or unreadable, or the masks couldn't be written. Fix the cause and choose **Analyze Now**. |
| **No picture to analyze** | The clip plays no frame of its file. |
| **Off** | Remove Background is off. |
| **—** | Several clips are selected. The section's header then reads "on". |

### Analyze Now

**Analyze Now** asks again for the masks the clip needs, then retries a run that failed. It's enabled only while a clip is analysing or has failed.

## Pictures

<Shot
  name="05k-clip-background-picture.inspector"
  alt="The Background section for an image clip. Remove background is ticked, a Subject row reads Foreground above Background, which reads Remove, then Edge, Feather and a Status of Analyzing 0 %."
/>

A picture gets one mask, made once on this Mac from the picture as the preview draws it, the right way up. Because it's one frame, **Status** goes straight from Analyzing to **Ready**.

**Person** uses the same person segmentation as a video. **Foreground** uses Vision's foreground instance mask, which keeps every foreground subject it finds. If it finds none, **Status** reads **No subject found** and the picture draws whole.

## Exports

An export draws the subject alone in every frame, GIF and APNG included. It waits at "Preparing…" until every mask it draws is made, with no time limit, and you can cancel it while it waits.

If a mask can't be made, the export fails with "Clip n's person masks could not be made: …" and writes no file. For a picture with **Subject** set to **Foreground**, the message says "foreground masks".

A single frame doesn't wait as long. **File ▸ Save Frame…** (<kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>) waits up to 30 seconds for the masks it needs. If they aren't ready by then, it saves the frame with the clip whole, and a sheet titled "Saved without Remove Background" names the files drawn whole. An agent's [`render_frame`](/mcp/render-frame/) waits the same 30 seconds and says so in its answer.

## Good to know

- A clip draws whole only when no frame it plays has a person. If the person leaves the picture for part of a clip, those frames have little or nothing to keep, so what's behind shows through.
- The recorder panel can do this for you. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).

## With an agent

An agent turns this on with `set_video`, as the checkbox does. `analyze_cutout` can wait up to 60 seconds for a clip's masks to settle, and it answers the subject's mean centre in the picture, which the app doesn't show. For a video, `get_media_analysis` says which stretches of the file hold a person. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).

## Related

- [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/)
- [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/)
- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
- [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/)

  alt="The Background section of the inspector, open, with its summary reading Analyzing 0 %. Remove background is ticked, Background reads Remove, Edge is at 0.00, Feather is at 0%, Status reads Analyzing 0 %, and an Analyze Now button sits below."
/>

## Turn it on

Select a clip and choose **Clip ▸ Remove Background**, or tick **Remove background** in the Clip tab's **Background** section. The menu item has no keyboard shortcut. Frame Job starts making the [masks](#how-the-masks-are-made) straight away, and you don't need to do anything else.

It works on clips of a video file with pictures, freeze frames of one, and image clips. Text, shape, graphic, adjustment and nest clips can't be cut out, and the section appears only when every selected clip can.

With several clips selected:

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Clip ▸ Remove Background** | When every clip that can be cut out already is, it turns them all off. Otherwise it turns on the ones without it, and each clip that has it keeps its own values. Selected clips that can't be cut out are left alone. |
| **Remove background** checkbox | Ticking it gives each clip without it the defaults. Unticking it removes it from all of them. |

The menu item shows a check when every target is cut out, a dash when some are, and nothing when none are. It's dimmed when no selected clip can be cut out. Either way, the change is one undo step, **Remove Background**.

The section comes right after **Chroma Key** and is shut by default. Its header reads "off", the [Status](#status), or "on" with several clips selected. **Reset** turns Remove Background off.

**Subject**, **Background**, **Edge** and **Feather** stay dimmed until every selected clip has Remove Background on. A selection where only some clips have it keeps them dimmed.

## Tune the cut-out

### Subject

This row shows only when every selected clip is a picture. See [Pictures](#pictures).

| Choice | What it keeps |
| --- | --- |
| **Person** (default) | The person |
| **Foreground** | The foreground subject, whatever it is: a person, a pet or an object |

It reads mixed when the selected pictures differ. A clip of a video file or a freeze frame always keeps the person.

### Background

**Remove**, the default, draws the subject alone. **Keep** draws the whole clip, while the subject still counts as a shape, and the masks are made either way.

**Keep** is how a title goes behind a person in frame, and it's what [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) gives a clip with no cut-out.

### Edge

Pulls the outline in or pushes it out. Below 0 pulls in, and above 0 pushes out. The range is −1 to 1, the default is 0, and the quick picks are −0.5, −0.25, 0, 0.25 and 0.5.

A mask is more or less sure of each point in the picture. **Edge** sets how sure it has to be. With **Feather** at 0:

| Edge | The outline sits where the mask is |
| --- | --- |
| −1 | 7/8 sure it's the person |
| −0.5 | 3/4 sure |
| 0 | Half sure |
| 0.5 | 1/4 sure |
| 1 | 1/8 sure |

Across a band of pixels where the mask fades from background to person, **Edge** at −1 or 1 moves the outline about three eighths of the band's width. Raising **Edge** never removes anything a lower value kept.

### Feather

How soft the outline is. The range is 0 to 100 %, the default is 0 %, and the quick picks are 0, 10, 25 and 50.

### Inside an action

With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Edge** and **Feather** set the value at the action's end and animate toward it. **Background** switches at the action's end, and its row shows "at end".

The **Remove background** checkbox and **Subject** always change the clip itself, even with an action selected, so their rows show ⊘. You can't turn a cut-out off at the end of an action.

## How the masks are made

A mask is the outline of the subject in one frame. You never start this yourself. Turning Remove Background on, or changing what a cut-out clip plays, asks for the frames that clip needs, and Frame Job makes them in the background while you go on working.

Masks are made on this Mac with Vision's person segmentation at its balanced setting. Nothing is uploaded, and no key is needed. They're kept per media in the project's cache, so a frame that's been analysed is never analysed again. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#person-masks).

Until a frame has its mask, the clip draws whole in the preview. A paused frame redraws by itself as masks land, and a playing preview picks them up on its next frame.

### Status

**Status** says where the clip's masks stand, and why a clip is drawing whole.

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Analyzing N %** | The masks are being made. The figure stops at 99 until they're done. |
| **Ready** | Every frame the clip plays has its mask. |
| **No person found** | Every frame was looked at and no person is in the clip, so it draws whole. A frame counts as holding a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half. |
| **No subject found** | A picture with **Subject** set to **Foreground** was looked at and no subject was found, so it draws whole. |
| **Failed:** and the reason | The masks couldn't be made. The media file may be missing or unreadable, or the masks couldn't be written. Fix the cause and choose **Analyze Now**. |
| **No picture to analyze** | The clip plays no frame of its file. |
| **Off** | Remove Background is off. |
| **—** | Several clips are selected. The section's header then reads "on". |

### Analyze Now

**Analyze Now** asks again for the masks the clip needs, then retries a run that failed. It's enabled only while a clip is analysing or has failed.

## Pictures

<Shot
  name="05k-clip-background-picture.inspector"
  alt="The Background section for an image clip. Remove background is ticked, a Subject row reads Foreground above Background, which reads Remove, then Edge, Feather and a Status of Analyzing 0 %."
/>

A picture gets one mask, made once on this Mac from the picture as the preview draws it, the right way up. Because it's one frame, **Status** goes straight from Analyzing to **Ready**.

**Person** uses the same person segmentation as a video. **Foreground** uses Vision's foreground instance mask, which keeps every foreground subject it finds. If it finds none, **Status** reads **No subject found** and the picture draws whole.

## Exports

An export draws the subject alone in every frame, GIF and APNG included. It waits at "Preparing…" until every mask it draws is made, with no time limit, and you can cancel it while it waits.

If a mask can't be made, the export fails with "Clip n's person masks could not be made: …" and writes no file. For a picture with **Subject** set to **Foreground**, the message says "foreground masks".

A single frame doesn't wait as long. **File ▸ Save Frame…** (<kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>) waits up to 30 seconds for the masks it needs. If they aren't ready by then, it saves the frame with the clip whole, and a sheet titled "Saved without Remove Background" names the files drawn whole. An agent's [`render_frame`](/mcp/render-frame/) waits the same 30 seconds and says so in its answer.

## Good to know

- A clip draws whole only when no frame it plays has a person. If the person leaves the picture for part of a clip, those frames have little or nothing to keep, so what's behind shows through.
- The recorder panel can do this for you. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).

## With an agent

An agent turns this on with `set_video`, as the checkbox does. `analyze_cutout` can wait up to 60 seconds for a clip's masks to settle, and it answers the subject's mean centre in the picture, which the app doesn't show. For a video, `get_media_analysis` says which stretches of the file hold a person. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).

## Related

- [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/)
- [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/)
- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
- [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/)

---
title: Text Behind Subject
description: Put a title, shape, picture or graphic behind the person in a clip, so they stand in front of it and the room stays behind it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Text Behind Subject puts a title behind the person in a camera clip or photo. The person stands in front of the title, and the room stays behind it. A shape, picture or graphic can go behind a person the same way.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject"
  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Behind Subject"
  tools={['text_behind_subject', 'set_video']}
  needs="Nothing. The masks are made on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Text behind subject in one step

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to where the title should start, over the camera clip or photo.

2. If several clips play there, select the one with the person.

3. Choose **Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject**. It has no keyboard shortcut.

4. The new title is selected, so type your text in the [Text tab](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/).

</Steps>

One **Undo** takes it all back. The step is named **Text Behind Subject**.

Here's what the command does:

- It adds a track named "Behind Subject" directly above the clip's track, and above any [matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/) in front of it.
- It puts a title on that track with the **Title** [preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/), running from the playhead for 4 seconds, or to the clip's end if that's sooner.
- It puts the title behind the subject.
- If the clip had no [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/), it turns that on with **Background** set to **Keep** and **Subject** set to **Person**, so the picture stays whole and the person still hides the title. A clip that already has a cut-out keeps it.

It works with a clip of a video file or a picture that's playing at the playhead, with its picture on, on a shown track that isn't a matte track. Of those, it takes the front-most selected clip, else the front-most with Remove Background on, else the front-most.

The item is greyed while a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open, and when no such clip plays at the playhead.

## Behind subject by hand

Any clip that draws can go behind a subject, except an adjustment clip or a nest clip.

<Steps>

1. Turn on [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) for the camera clip. Set **Background** to **Keep** if you want the room to stay.

2. Put the clip you want behind the person on a track in front of the camera clip, and select it.

3. In the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, open the **Behind Subject** section and tick **Behind subject**.

</Steps>

The section comes right after **Transform** and is shut by default. Its header reads "on" or "off". The box is off by default, and it's one undo step, **Behind Subject**. **Reset** turns it off, and the box reads mixed over a selection that disagrees.

With one clip selected and the box on, the section says "No cut-out clip is behind it at the playhead." when nothing cuts the clip there.

With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, the box sets the action's end, and the clip switches at the action's end. The row shows "at end".

The section isn't offered while a nest is open.

## What cuts the clip

A clip with **Behind subject** on is cut, at every moment, by the person in every cut-out clip on a track behind it. Any clip with Remove Background on counts, with **Background** set to **Remove** or **Keep**.

Clip order decides it. A cut-out clip on a track in front of the clip doesn't cut it.

Where no person mask is drawn yet, or no person is found, the clip draws whole. See [How the masks are made](/effects/remove-background/#how-the-masks-are-made).

## Good to know

- A subject inside a nest cuts a top-level title when the nest clip is behind the title. A top-level camera never cuts a title inside a nest, because a nest is one picture to the timeline.
- The clip's [shadow](/effects/shadow/) is cut with it.
- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) draws sharp on a clip cut this way, and on the person drawn over it.

## With an agent

`text_behind_subject` does what the menu item does, and it can also take the title's text, its start time and the clip to go behind. It works on the top-level timeline only, and it leaves the selection as it was. An agent can also set the flag inside a nest with `set_video`, where the section isn't offered, and it works among the clips of that nest. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Related

- [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/)
- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
- [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/)
- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)

---
title: Shadow
description: Add a drop shadow cast by a clip's own shape, and set its colour, strength, softness, direction and distance.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A drop shadow lifts a clip off what's behind it. It's cast by the clip's own shape: the picture, a text clip's letters, or a shape's outline and fill.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Shadow" tools="set_video" />

## Drop shadow

Select a clip, open the **Shadow** section in the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, and tick **Drop shadow**. It's off by default, and every clip that draws has it, text, shapes and graphics included.

Turning it on gives a soft shadow, down and to the right: black at 50 % with a 12 px blur, at 315° and 8 px away. The other rows stay dimmed until it's on.

The section's header reads "off", or the blur in pixels. **Reset** takes the shadow off.

The shadow follows what the clip actually draws. A clip with a [key](/effects/chroma-key/) or [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) casts the shadow of what's left, and the shadow fades with the clip's [opacity](/canvas/transform/).

## Shape the shadow

### Color

Any colour, black by default. A colour you can see through multiplies with **Opacity**, so the shadow gets fainter than **Opacity** alone says.

In an HLG project, shadow colours are lifted with the other drawn colours. See [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).

### Opacity

The shadow's strength. The range is 0 to 100 %, the default is 50 %, and the quick picks are 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100.

### Blur

How soft the shadow is. The range is 0 to 200 px, the default is 12 px, and the quick picks are 0, 4, 8, 12, 24 and 48.

The pixels are the clip's own, so the blur grows when you scale the clip up.

### Angle

Which way the shadow falls. The range is 0 to 360°, the default is 315°, and the quick picks run every 45°.

0° is to the right, and the angle increases counter-clockwise, so 90° is up, 180° is left, 270° is down and 315° is down and to the right.

The direction belongs to the canvas, not the clip. Rotating a clip doesn't turn its shadow, so every shadow at the same angle falls the same way.

### Distance

How far the shadow falls from the clip. The range is 0 to 200 px, the default is 8 px, and the quick picks are 0, 4, 8, 16 and 32.

Like **Blur**, it's in the clip's own pixels, so it grows when you scale the clip up.

## Animate a shadow

With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Color**, **Opacity**, **Blur**, **Angle** and **Distance** set the value at the action's end and animate toward it. The colour blends through the OKLab colour space. Unticking **Drop shadow** with an action selected turns the shadow off at the action's end.

## Good to know

- A shadow has no effect on a clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/). The settings are kept and apply again when the track stops being a matte.
- A clip with [Behind subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) on has its shadow cut with it.
- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) draws sharp under a drop shadow.

## Related

- [Reflection](/effects/reflection/)
- [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/)
- [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/)

---
title: Chroma Key
description: Remove a background colour, such as a green screen, so whatever is on the tracks behind shows through.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Chroma Key removes one colour from a clip, such as a green screen, so whatever is on the tracks behind shows through.

<AtAGlance
  keys="⎋"
  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Chroma Key"
  tools="set_video"
/>

## Key out a color

<Steps>

1. Put the clip on a track in front of what should show through, and select it.

2. In the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, open the **Chroma Key** section. It comes after **Corner Radius** and is shut by default.

3. Choose **Pick from Canvas** and click the background in the preview. That sets the colour and turns the key on. Or tick **Key out a color**, which keys pure green.

4. Adjust [**Tolerance**](#tolerance), [**Softness**](#softness) and [**Spill**](#spill) until the edges look right.

</Steps>

Turning the key on gives pure green at 20 % Tolerance, 10 % Softness and 50 % Spill. Every row but **Pick from Canvas** stays dimmed until the key is on. The section's header reads "off", or the Tolerance as a percentage. **Reset** takes the key off the clip.

The section is there for clips of a video file, image clips and freeze frames. Text, shape and graphic clips don't have it. With several clips selected, an edit keys all of them.

## Key color

The colour to remove. It starts as pure green, and the swatch takes any colour. The opacity in the colour panel has no effect here, because a key colour has none.

## Pick from Canvas

Choose **Pick from Canvas** and the preview reads "Click to pick the key color · Esc to cancel". One click on the picture sets **Key Color**. The button works with the key off, and a pick turns it on.

A pick reads the clip as the key sees it, without the clip's own key, grade and opacity. So picking again reads the same green the first pick did, even though that green is now a hole. A clip in front of it at that point still covers it, and you get what's visible there.

Picking again changes only the colour. It keeps the **Tolerance**, **Softness** and **Spill** you set.

To cancel, press the button again, press <kbd>⎋</kbd> or change the selection.

| If | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| You click outside the picture | Frame Job beeps and stays ready for another click |
| You click where the canvas holds nothing | Frame Job beeps and changes nothing |
| The selection changes while the frame is being read | Frame Job beeps and changes nothing |

Only one canvas tool is ready at a time. **Pick from Canvas** ends [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)'s **Place on Canvas**, [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) and the [qualifier's Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/).

## Tune the key

Start with **Tolerance** to clear the background, then **Softness** for the edge, then **Spill** for any fringe of the key colour.

### Tolerance

How far from the key colour still counts as background. Everything that close is removed completely. Raise it if patches of background remain, and lower it if the key eats into your subject.

The range is 0 to 100 %, and the default is 20 %. The quick picks are 0, 10, 20, 40 and 60.

### Softness

How gradual the edge of the key is. Past **Tolerance**, the picture fades back in over this distance, so a low value gives a hard edge.

The range is 0 to 100 %, and the default is 10 %. The quick picks are 0, 5, 10, 25 and 50.

### Spill

How much of the key colour is removed from the edges that remain. Pixels in the soft edge are pulled toward a grey of their own brightness, which takes out a green fringe. It works only in that edge, so with **Softness** at 0 it has almost nothing to act on.

The range is 0 to 100 %, and the default is 50 %. The quick picks are 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100.

## Animate the key

With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Key Color**, **Tolerance**, **Softness** and **Spill** set the value at the action's end and animate toward it. The colour blends through the OKLab colour space along the action. **Pick from Canvas** also sends its colour to the action's end.

## Good to know

- The key runs before the grade, so [grading a clip](/color/color-tab/) doesn't change what's keyed. A [camera log](/hdr/camera-log/) conversion and the [source conversion](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/) come first, so the key sees the converted picture.
- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) leaves the key on.
- How a key behaves when a project switches between SDR and HDR is on [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).

## Related

- [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/)

---
title: Remove Background
description: Keep the person in a video or picture and make the rest transparent, with no green screen, upload or key.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Remove Background keeps the person in a video or picture and makes the rest transparent, so whatever is on the tracks behind shows through. You don't need a green screen.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Background"
  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Background"
  tools={['set_video', 'analyze_cutout', 'get_media_analysis']}
  needs="Nothing. The masks are made on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

<Shot
  name="05i-clip-background.inspector"
  alt="The Background section of the inspector, open, with its summary reading Analyzing 0 %. Remove background is ticked, Background reads Remove, Edge is at 0.00, Feather is at 0%, Status reads Analyzing 0 %, and an Analyze Now button sits below."
/>

## Turn it on

Select a clip and choose **Clip ▸ Remove Background**, or tick **Remove background** in the Clip tab's **Background** section. The menu item has no keyboard shortcut. Frame Job starts making the [masks](#how-the-masks-are-made) straight away, and you don't need to do anything else.

It works on clips of a video file with pictures, freeze frames of one, and image clips. Text, shape, graphic, adjustment and nest clips can't be cut out, and the section appears only when every selected clip can.

With several clips selected:

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Clip ▸ Remove Background** | When every clip that can be cut out already is, it turns them all off. Otherwise it turns on the ones without it, and each clip that has it keeps its own values. Selected clips that can't be cut out are left alone. |
| **Remove background** checkbox | Ticking it gives each clip without it the defaults. Unticking it removes it from all of them. |

The menu item shows a check when every target is cut out, a dash when some are, and nothing when none are. It's dimmed when no selected clip can be cut out. Either way, the change is one undo step, **Remove Background**.

The section comes right after **Chroma Key** and is shut by default. Its header reads "off", the [Status](#status), or "on" with several clips selected. **Reset** turns Remove Background off.

**Subject**, **Background**, **Edge** and **Feather** stay dimmed until every selected clip has Remove Background on. A selection where only some clips have it keeps them dimmed.

## Tune the cut-out

### Subject

This row shows only when every selected clip is a picture. See [Pictures](#pictures).

| Choice | What it keeps |
| --- | --- |
| **Person** (default) | The person |
| **Foreground** | The foreground subject, whatever it is: a person, a pet or an object |

It reads mixed when the selected pictures differ. A clip of a video file or a freeze frame always keeps the person.

### Background

**Remove**, the default, draws the subject alone. **Keep** draws the whole clip, while the subject still counts as a shape, and the masks are made either way.

**Keep** is how a title goes behind a person in frame, and it's what [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) gives a clip with no cut-out.

### Edge

Pulls the outline in or pushes it out. Below 0 pulls in, and above 0 pushes out. The range is −1 to 1, the default is 0, and the quick picks are −0.5, −0.25, 0, 0.25 and 0.5.

A mask is more or less sure of each point in the picture. **Edge** sets how sure it has to be. With **Feather** at 0:

| Edge | The outline sits where the mask is |
| --- | --- |
| −1 | 7/8 sure it's the person |
| −0.5 | 3/4 sure |
| 0 | Half sure |
| 0.5 | 1/4 sure |
| 1 | 1/8 sure |

Across a band of pixels where the mask fades from background to person, **Edge** at −1 or 1 moves the outline about three eighths of the band's width. Raising **Edge** never removes anything a lower value kept.

### Feather

How soft the outline is. The range is 0 to 100 %, the default is 0 %, and the quick picks are 0, 10, 25 and 50.

### Inside an action

With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Edge** and **Feather** set the value at the action's end and animate toward it. **Background** switches at the action's end, and its row shows "at end".

The **Remove background** checkbox and **Subject** always change the clip itself, even with an action selected, so their rows show ⊘. You can't turn a cut-out off at the end of an action.

## How the masks are made

A mask is the outline of the subject in one frame. You never start this yourself. Turning Remove Background on, or changing what a cut-out clip plays, asks for the frames that clip needs, and Frame Job makes them in the background while you go on working.

Masks are made on this Mac with Vision's person segmentation at its balanced setting. Nothing is uploaded, and no key is needed. They're kept per media in the project's cache, so a frame that's been analysed is never analysed again. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#person-masks).

Until a frame has its mask, the clip draws whole in the preview. A paused frame redraws by itself as masks land, and a playing preview picks them up on its next frame.

### Status

**Status** says where the clip's masks stand, and why a clip is drawing whole.

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Analyzing N %** | The masks are being made. The figure stops at 99 until they're done. |
| **Ready** | Every frame the clip plays has its mask. |
| **No person found** | Every frame was looked at and no person is in the clip, so it draws whole. A frame counts as holding a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half. |
| **No subject found** | A picture with **Subject** set to **Foreground** was looked at and no subject was found, so it draws whole. |
| **Failed:** and the reason | The masks couldn't be made. The media file may be missing or unreadable, or the masks couldn't be written. Fix the cause and choose **Analyze Now**. |
| **No picture to analyze** | The clip plays no frame of its file. |
| **Off** | Remove Background is off. |
| **—** | Several clips are selected. The section's header then reads "on". |

### Analyze Now

**Analyze Now** asks again for the masks the clip needs, then retries a run that failed. It's enabled only while a clip is analysing or has failed.

## Pictures

<Shot
  name="05k-clip-background-picture.inspector"
  alt="The Background section for an image clip. Remove background is ticked, a Subject row reads Foreground above Background, which reads Remove, then Edge, Feather and a Status of Analyzing 0 %."
/>

A picture gets one mask, made once on this Mac from the picture as the preview draws it, the right way up. Because it's one frame, **Status** goes straight from Analyzing to **Ready**.

**Person** uses the same person segmentation as a video. **Foreground** uses Vision's foreground instance mask, which keeps every foreground subject it finds. If it finds none, **Status** reads **No subject found** and the picture draws whole.

## Exports

An export draws the subject alone in every frame, GIF and APNG included. It waits at "Preparing…" until every mask it draws is made, with no time limit, and you can cancel it while it waits.

If a mask can't be made, the export fails with "Clip n's person masks could not be made: …" and writes no file. For a picture with **Subject** set to **Foreground**, the message says "foreground masks".

A single frame doesn't wait as long. **File ▸ Save Frame…** (<kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>) waits up to 30 seconds for the masks it needs. If they aren't ready by then, it saves the frame with the clip whole, and a sheet titled "Saved without Remove Background" names the files drawn whole. An agent's [`render_frame`](/mcp/render-frame/) waits the same 30 seconds and says so in its answer.

## Good to know

- A clip draws whole only when no frame it plays has a person. If the person leaves the picture for part of a clip, those frames have little or nothing to keep, so what's behind shows through.
- The recorder panel can do this for you. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).

## With an agent

An agent turns this on with `set_video`, as the checkbox does. `analyze_cutout` can wait up to 60 seconds for a clip's masks to settle, and it answers the subject's mean centre in the picture, which the app doesn't show. For a video, `get_media_analysis` says which stretches of the file hold a person. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).

## Related

- [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/)
- [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/)
- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
- [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/)

---
title: Text Behind Subject
description: Put a title, shape, picture or graphic behind the person in a clip, so they stand in front of it and the room stays behind it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Text Behind Subject puts a title behind the person in a camera clip or photo. The person stands in front of the title, and the room stays behind it. A shape, picture or graphic can go behind a person the same way.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject"
  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Behind Subject"
  tools={['text_behind_subject', 'set_video']}
  needs="Nothing. The masks are made on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Text behind subject in one step

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to where the title should start, over the camera clip or photo.

2. If several clips play there, select the one with the person.

3. Choose **Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject**. It has no keyboard shortcut.

4. The new title is selected, so type your text in the [Text tab](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/).

</Steps>

One **Undo** takes it all back. The step is named **Text Behind Subject**.

Here's what the command does:

- It adds a track named "Behind Subject" directly above the clip's track, and above any [matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/) in front of it.
- It puts a title on that track with the **Title** [preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/), running from the playhead for 4 seconds, or to the clip's end if that's sooner.
- It puts the title behind the subject.
- If the clip had no [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/), it turns that on with **Background** set to **Keep** and **Subject** set to **Person**, so the picture stays whole and the person still hides the title. A clip that already has a cut-out keeps it.

It works with a clip of a video file or a picture that's playing at the playhead, with its picture on, on a shown track that isn't a matte track. Of those, it takes the front-most selected clip, else the front-most with Remove Background on, else the front-most.

The item is greyed while a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open, and when no such clip plays at the playhead.

## Behind subject by hand

Any clip that draws can go behind a subject, except an adjustment clip or a nest clip.

<Steps>

1. Turn on [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) for the camera clip. Set **Background** to **Keep** if you want the room to stay.

2. Put the clip you want behind the person on a track in front of the camera clip, and select it.

3. In the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, open the **Behind Subject** section and tick **Behind subject**.

</Steps>

The section comes right after **Transform** and is shut by default. Its header reads "on" or "off". The box is off by default, and it's one undo step, **Behind Subject**. **Reset** turns it off, and the box reads mixed over a selection that disagrees.

With one clip selected and the box on, the section says "No cut-out clip is behind it at the playhead." when nothing cuts the clip there.

With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, the box sets the action's end, and the clip switches at the action's end. The row shows "at end".

The section isn't offered while a nest is open.

## What cuts the clip

A clip with **Behind subject** on is cut, at every moment, by the person in every cut-out clip on a track behind it. Any clip with Remove Background on counts, with **Background** set to **Remove** or **Keep**.

Clip order decides it. A cut-out clip on a track in front of the clip doesn't cut it.

Where no person mask is drawn yet, or no person is found, the clip draws whole. See [How the masks are made](/effects/remove-background/#how-the-masks-are-made).

## Good to know

- A subject inside a nest cuts a top-level title when the nest clip is behind the title. A top-level camera never cuts a title inside a nest, because a nest is one picture to the timeline.
- The clip's [shadow](/effects/shadow/) is cut with it.
- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) draws sharp on a clip cut this way, and on the person drawn over it.

## With an agent

`text_behind_subject` does what the menu item does, and it can also take the title's text, its start time and the clip to go behind. It works on the top-level timeline only, and it leaves the selection as it was. An agent can also set the flag inside a nest with `set_video`, where the section isn't offered, and it works among the clips of that nest. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Related

- [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/)
- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
- [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/)
- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)

---
title: Shadow
description: Add a drop shadow cast by a clip's own shape, and set its colour, strength, softness, direction and distance.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A drop shadow lifts a clip off what's behind it. It's cast by the clip's own shape: the picture, a text clip's letters, or a shape's outline and fill.

<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Shadow" tools="set_video" />

## Drop shadow

Select a clip, open the **Shadow** section in the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, and tick **Drop shadow**. It's off by default, and every clip that draws has it, text, shapes and graphics included.

Turning it on gives a soft shadow, down and to the right: black at 50 % with a 12 px blur, at 315° and 8 px away. The other rows stay dimmed until it's on.

The section's header reads "off", or the blur in pixels. **Reset** takes the shadow off.

The shadow follows what the clip actually draws. A clip with a [key](/effects/chroma-key/) or [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) casts the shadow of what's left, and the shadow fades with the clip's [opacity](/canvas/transform/).

## Shape the shadow

### Color

Any colour, black by default. A colour you can see through multiplies with **Opacity**, so the shadow gets fainter than **Opacity** alone says.

In an HLG project, shadow colours are lifted with the other drawn colours. See [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).

### Opacity

The shadow's strength. The range is 0 to 100 %, the default is 50 %, and the quick picks are 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100.

### Blur

How soft the shadow is. The range is 0 to 200 px, the default is 12 px, and the quick picks are 0, 4, 8, 12, 24 and 48.

The pixels are the clip's own, so the blur grows when you scale the clip up.

### Angle

Which way the shadow falls. The range is 0 to 360°, the default is 315°, and the quick picks run every 45°.

0° is to the right, and the angle increases counter-clockwise, so 90° is up, 180° is left, 270° is down and 315° is down and to the right.

The direction belongs to the canvas, not the clip. Rotating a clip doesn't turn its shadow, so every shadow at the same angle falls the same way.

### Distance

How far the shadow falls from the clip. The range is 0 to 200 px, the default is 8 px, and the quick picks are 0, 4, 8, 16 and 32.

Like **Blur**, it's in the clip's own pixels, so it grows when you scale the clip up.

## Animate a shadow

With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Color**, **Opacity**, **Blur**, **Angle** and **Distance** set the value at the action's end and animate toward it. The colour blends through the OKLab colour space. Unticking **Drop shadow** with an action selected turns the shadow off at the action's end.

## Good to know

- A shadow has no effect on a clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/). The settings are kept and apply again when the track stops being a matte.
- A clip with [Behind subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) on has its shadow cut with it.
- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) draws sharp under a drop shadow.

## Related

- [Reflection](/effects/reflection/)
- [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/)
- [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/)
